name: engine-unity
description: Unity for Studio (Unity 6 / 6000.x LTS, on the host where Unity Hub is; never in a sandbox): the unity tool finds the Hub, the editors, their build modules and the licence; makes 2D, 2.5D and 3D projects from the editor's templates (URP or built-in) with the harness bridge package (com.harness.bridge) and test assemblies, and Studio's .studio/project.json; describes projects; runs C# headless (-batchmode -executeMethod) or live in the open editor through a localhost, token-protected bridge (scene, GameObjects, components, prefabs, play mode, captures, the console); imports and exports assets (FBX, glTF through glTFast, textures and sprite sheets, audio); captures and renders frames; builds levels from grid layouts (tilemaps, isometric, 3D) with collect-and-escape rules; runs Unity Test Framework tests with parsed results; builds and packages Windows 64-bit and WebGL players with the build report; plays the game N seconds with an input timeline (frames, fps, memory, draw calls, events, a Studio playtest) and drives it step by step for the AI player (driver.mjs). Heavy work runs through Studio's job queue. Gates unity-project, unity-tests, unity-build; skills unity-essentials, unity-csharp, unity-2d, unity-build-test; the unity-engineer agent. Installing editors, accepting EULAs and activating the licence are the person's, in Unity Hub.
